label: sequence started with k: late original positions and <DEL>
explanation: Fires when the first original token is k (first_tok=k has 22.6x lift and holds 95% of activation mass), from original step 3 through the <DEL> step. It is silent at t=0-2 and nearly silent through the copy phase (138 activations, tiny); at <DEL> the output is k (orig(0)), which is why out_tok=k shows high lift. Activation tends to build over steps 3-5 and stays high until <DEL>, which is somewhat weaker. The strongest examples begin with k k, but requiring orig(1)=k catches only 2% of activations, so a second k is not needed. Missed activations (5% of mass) are weak firings in sequences that do not start with k, often with k at position 1. False positives are mostly the step-3 token, where activation is still near zero.

issues: Count recall is only 0.756 (test), and activation-quartile coverage is just 0.24 for the weakest quartile. Missed steps make up about 24% of active steps, but they carry only 5.2% of activation mass on test (mass recall 0.948). Example misses with activation around 0.02-0.3: 'j k m w v [k:0.06]...', 'w k b e t [o:0.12] [2:0.22]...'.

The largest miss class is systematic, not scattered: first_tok!=k & orig(1)==k & t>=3 & phase<=1 covers 14.1% of all activations (about 60% of the misses) but only 4.1% of mass. Its precision is only 0.19 and varies a lot with first_tok (r/2/w/t about 0.5; c/f/i/x/0 about 0). It can't be added to the predicate: the OR version scores test F1 0.680. The explanation already names this class ('often with k at position 1'), so it is disclosed, not hidden.
The remaining misses (about 9% of activations and 1.1% of mass, in sequences with no k at all) are weak scattered noise.

Claims check out. Zero activations at t=0-2. Copy phase: 138 activations, and the k-start & phase==2 slice has precision 0.0. Within k-start sequences, precision is 0.83 at t=3 (onset, the source of most false positives) and about 1.0 at t>=4 and at <DEL> when L>=5. At <DEL>, precision drops at L=3 (0.66, n=428), which is minor.

Small overstatement: 'strongest examples begin with k k'. Within k-start sequences, orig(1)==k gives slightly lower precision (0.817 vs 0.963), so a second k does not make firing more reliable. This is minor.
Dropping t==3 (t>=4) raises precision to 0.997 but cuts test F1 to 0.758, so the original predicate is better.
